author: Codex in this conversation
kind: Methodological review of the actual Lyra output; not an independent blinded model benchmark

findings.title: Keep the evidence question explicit
findings.observation: The model maps ‘How can we tell?’ mainly to time horizon. The final seven axes have no explicit evidence-standard dimension.
findings.proposal: Retain a cross-cutting evidence contract: causal versus observational evidence; biomarkers versus clinical events; absolute effect and uncertainty; confounding; funding; overlapping cohorts; replication. Do not pretend this evidence has already been collected.

findings.title: Separate risk prediction from treatment-response prediction
findings.observation: The individual-differences axis lists clinical groups, but does not distinguish baseline risk from predictors of the effect of changing egg intake.
findings.proposal: Ask whether each candidate predicts baseline outcome risk, a reproducible within-person lipid response, or an externally validated difference in the effect of egg intake. Record interaction uncertainty; subgroup differences alone do not establish a predictor.

findings.title: Do not let list order choose the research question
findings.observation: The assembler automatically marks the first option kept. In this run that includes cardiovascular mortality, less than one egg per week, and replacing processed/red meat.
findings.proposal: Treat these as model defaults, not user-approved choices. This artifact starts every dimension unresolved. Ask whether the investigation is general or personal before asking for medical context.

findings.title: Separate attributes that can coexist
findings.observation: ‘Whole eggs’ and ‘cooked with little added fat’ appear as alternative branches, although both can describe the same meal. Health outcomes and broader tradeoffs overlap too.
findings.proposal: Use independent exposure fields for yolk/white, cooking, accompanying foods, and addition versus substitution. Allow multiple outcome families in the research portfolio without merging them into one goodness score.

findings.title: Preserve inferred versus explicit cues
findings.observation: The comparator is grounded in ‘What else should we be paying attention to here?’ rather than an explicit comparator in the question.
findings.proposal: Label the comparator as a method-required inference. Exact substring matching verifies quotation integrity; it does not establish that the attached interpretation follows from the quote.

next_context_question: Is this a general evidence map to share with others, or a decision about what you personally should eat?
